lines.caption: This is a tour of pull request 98, which stops an agent replying to every CI event while you're there, and gives times in Pacific time.
It has three parts: what the PR adds, how it was checked, and what comes later.
Part 1. What this PR adds.
Three new rules for working with you, two old lines pointed at them, and a new first step for the build-verify agent.
First, a routine event wakes the agent: a CI comment edited mid-run, a check still running, an older head, or its own echo.
The agent reads it and ends the turn with one short line, never an empty turn, without repeating its question.
Only real news gets a message: a pass or fail, a blocker, a merge, a new question, or a comment from you.
Second, when a question waits for you, the agent asks it once.
It stops watching the PR and schedules a check-in, about 50 minutes later, then every 4 hours.
Once you answer, it cancels the check-in, watches the PR again, and checks what landed through pr-digest.
Third, before a build in a cloud container, the build-verify agent hides its build outputs from git, in that clone only.
So the Stop hook no longer warns about untracked files after every turn.
In session 74, every CI event got a reply that repeated the open question, and the thread kept scrolling.
Quiet means one short line, because an empty turn makes the harness ask for a reply.
An interactive session is any session where you answer in its chat. A check-in that pushed a fix is followed in about 50 minutes.
Whenever the orchestrator marks a batch row as waiting, it marks the session's title too, and clears the row once that mark is gone.
Step zero asks git where the exclude file is, creates its folder if needed, and adds each missing line.
A gitignore change would count as code, so CI would run a full build. The exclude file stays local.
A check-in still catches a CI result while the agent waits, at a set pace instead of a wake-up for every event.
This PR also closes issue 99: every time shown to you is in US Pacific time, never UTC alone.
lines.say: This PR also closes issue ninety-nine: every time shown to you is in US Pacific time, never U T C alone.

lines.caption: Here are the new lines in CLAUDE.md, shortened, with the check-in timing.
The PR changes CLAUDE.md, the build-verify agent and the batch skill. CLAUDE.md's Verify recipe now runs step zero first.
To undo it, revert the commit. Leftover exclude lines only hide build outputs.
Part 2. How it was built and verified.
Only instructions changed, so there was no Thunar build or screenshot. A fresh agent and CI's review checked it.
The rules follow the issue's wording, and session 74, which did the same steps by hand.
The exclude list was applied by hand in this clone, but no build was run, so it wasn't checked against one.
The local review found eight issues, and seven were fixed.
There's no verify script, since no code changed. On the first push, CI's build and verify skipped as no code changed, and passed.
CI's review of that push found nine issues, and eight were fixed.
The explainer job failed then, because this page wasn't pushed yet. CI's second review resolved R1 and found nine more.
On the second push, build, verify and the explainer passed. CI's third review resolved R2 and R10 and found eight more.
On the third push, everything else passed too. CI's fourth review resolved R19 to R22 and found six more.
CI's fifth review resolved R27 to R29 and found one more.
While that finding's question waited for you, this session followed the new rule: one check-in, nothing new, no message.
CI's sixth review resolved R33 and found five more.
CI's seventh review resolved R34 and found eight more.
CI's eighth review resolved five findings and found eight more.
Step zero's new snippet was run twice on this clone, and the exclude file stayed at 24 lines.
lines.say: Step zero's new snippet was run twice on this clone, and the exclude file stayed at twenty-four lines.

lines.caption: CI's ninth review passed, with no confirmed medium or high finding left, and found six low ones.
After round 9, the step zero snippet was run again: exit 0, and the exclude file still had 24 lines.
lines.say: After round nine, the step zero snippet was run again: exit zero, and the exclude file still had twenty-four lines.

lines.caption: CI's tenth review passed again and found six more low findings.
CI's eleventh review failed on one medium finding, caused by round ten's own fix.
CI's review of the round 11 fix passed, with six new low findings.
This page was rendered and its narration stamped by the explainer subagent.
The one high finding: the exclude list missed several build outputs. They were all added.
Two old lines contradicted the new rules and now point to them. Wording was tightened and a dead entry removed.
No check-in delay was named at first. CI's later review led to fixed delays.
CI's reviews found more findings on eleven pushes. The last one passed, and every confirmed finding is now fixed or resolved.
The first two medium ones: the check-in wasn't rescheduled, and resubscribing missed what landed meanwhile. Both are now fixed.
Your comments always get a reply, and CI's comments are still read only through the digest agent.
Step zero now asks git for the exclude file and runs only in the cloud.
Step zero now names issue 97, to make plain that the issue asked for it.
Next, check-ins got a pace and a limit, and are cancelled on your answer, a merge, or a new question.
A routine edit is now one made while its check still runs, and every quiet turn is exactly one short line.
Two low findings were accepted with a trailer: the output list is current, and the sandbox runs step zero anyway.
In round three, a check-in that acted on a CI result now schedules the next one while the question still waits.
The batch skill, the watch line and the Building section were brought in line with the new rules, refined again later.
Four more low findings were accepted with a trailer, each with its reason on the page.
In round four, two working check-ins clear a waiting batch row, and a check-in that pushed comes back in 50 minutes.
Three more low findings were accepted with a trailer, each with its reason on the page.
The last finding hit the batch line a third time. You chose CI's fix: the first working check-in is now recorded on the row.
A fourth finding hit that line. You chose to patch again, and round six replaced the guess with a direct check for your reply.
Eight more hit the batch line. You chose to patch again, and round seven has the waiting session mark its own title.
Round eight: you chose to patch a fourth time. The orchestrator now sets the title mark itself, and step zero became a snippet.
Three more low findings were accepted with a trailer, each with its reason on the page.
Round nine fixed five lows: an unmarked fallback, a mark added only once, a snippet that fails loudly, and the Verify recipe.
The last two were accepted with a trailer: issue 99 is here at your request, and a cleared row counts one check-in later by design.
lines.say: The last two were accepted with a trailer: issue ninety-nine is here at your request, and a cleared row counts one check-in later by design.

lines.caption: Round ten fixed five more lows, mostly tightening the batch skill's rows and rules.
Two more were accepted: unmarked rows clear only on the session's next message by design, and CI's own verifier disproved the other.
Round eleven fixed that by simplifying: every waiting row marks the title, and the working guess is gone.
The last six lows were accepted with a trailer, each with its reason on the page.
After the merge, the next batch shows whether questions stop repeating, and the next cloud build whether the Stop hook stays quiet.
Links go to the pull request, the issue, and the batch that runs it.
Part 3. What comes later.
No open issue builds on this one. The next batch is the first to run under these rules.
Its sessions read the new rules, and then you read their transcripts.
If a question repeats between two of your messages, that becomes a new issue.
In short: one short line for routine events, each question asked once, no build-file warnings, and times in Pacific time.
